title: Inside a mobile device
summary: Replace components with care and a plan.

passages.heading: The core idea
passages.markdown: A laptop packs familiar components into a small, model-specific enclosure. Its battery stores energy, its RAM holds active work, and its SSD retains files after shutdown. A slow system does not automatically need more storage: check whether memory pressure, a full drive, or thermal throttling explains the symptom. Before purchasing a replacement, consult the service guide for the exact model and confirm which components can actually be removed.

passages.heading: In the real world
passages.markdown: Prepare a clean workspace, shut down the device, disconnect external power, and follow the manufacturer’s battery-disconnection procedure before touching internal parts. Use suitable electrostatic-discharge protection and keep a record of screw positions. Handle memory by its edges rather than its contacts. Antenna leads and ribbon connectors are delicate; release their latches as documented instead of pulling harder. A swollen battery requires an approved safety procedure, never pressure or puncturing.

passages.heading: Make it stick
passages.markdown: Put it into practice by explaining the decision in your own words. In a support scenario, identify the requirement first, connect it to the relevant technology, and check the result against that requirement. If the evidence changes, revisit your reasoning rather than repeating the same action. Document what you observed so the next person can understand your conclusion.

options.whyWrong: This connects the requirement with the appropriate concept.
